role.altitude: The week stays in the classroom. Closed items and filing take less time. Remedial teaching, sitting a test, and encouraging a pupil stay with the teacher. The teacher still accepts every remedial program, every grade and every progress note. No tool sets a level or a mark.
reach: A teaching assistant runs the filed remedial program without rewriting the activities.
An instructional coordinator reuses the same goal codes when checking that a test matches the year plan.
skills_to_grow: Reject a drafted score when the answer does not show that rubric level.
Refuse a remedial activity that names a diagnosis the notes do not contain.
Offer a harder task without scoring the child's mood or face.
role.ambitious_version: Every pupil who misses a skill starts a short extra-help block that week, and every accepted grade is on the pupil record the next morning.

tasks.short: Prepare and run extra-help programs for pupils who need them.

steps.what: Note which students need extra help on a skill.
Read those students' marks in the pupil administration system.
Draft a remedial program for the named skill gap.

loop.input: Skill-gap note with pupil id, skill code and the teacher's words, plus the lesson goal code and recent marks.
loop.output: A short remedial program: activity titles, minutes and the same skill code, or a blank activity where the note is thin.
loop.check: The teacher reads each activity and rejects one that names a diagnosis or a support need the note does not state.
loop.stop: One pass. A rejected activity stays blank. No second call.
loop.why_not_simpler: The note is free text, so a fixed activity list cannot tell which practice this pupil needs.

steps.what: Talk that remedial program through with the parent.
Accept the remedial program before it is stored.
Store the accepted remedial program on the pupil file.
Implement that remedial program with the students.

tasks.design: The teacher notes the skill gap and reads marks in the {OTHER}, the pupil administration system. One pass drafts a remedial program from that note and the lesson goal; the teacher rejects a diagnosis the note does not state, talks with the parent, and accepts the program before it is stored. The teacher still runs the program with the pupils.
tasks.previous_blocker: The program was a stack of notes, and the activities were rewritten for each pupil by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded pass can draft activities from a note and a goal code, and the teacher can reject a line in one reading.
tasks.still_hard: Seeing what this pupil can manage this week, and whether the parent agrees, stays with the teacher.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher knows whether this child can face the extra practice without shame.

ambition.what: Start a short remedial block the same week the skill gap is noted.

tasks.altitude: Less time rewriting activities, the same time teaching the extra-help group. The teacher still accepts the program.

reach.task: Run the filed remedial activities with the group.
reach.learn: Use the accepted activities and minutes, and send back only what the pupil could not do.

evidence.claim: Snappet drafts a class activity for the lesson goal. The teacher still chooses whether it belongs in a remedial program.
Snappet's Copilot, piloted at Lucas Onderwijs, suggests arithmetic lessons the teacher accepts or changes.

Under the Dutch primary-education act, a formal development plan is set within six weeks of enrolment after consulting parents and is evaluated yearly. That rule applies when this extra help is that plan, not to every short practice block.
The works-councils act does not apply to schools. Under the school participation act, staff consent to tools that can monitor them, and parents and pupils consent to pupil-data rules.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes or sets the education level is high-risk. This draft does not set the pupil's level.

Pupil records rely on a public-task basis, and support needs in a formal plan can be health data, so a new store of those notes needs a data-protection assessment. Model knowledge, as stated in the digest.

assumptions: The focal boundary is the elementary teacher from the skill-gap note through the parent talk, the accepted program and the session they still teach. A teaching assistant who later runs a session is out of this task's time.

Fields are pupil id, skill code, lesson goal code, note text, activity title, minutes, parent consulted yes or no, and the accepted version. The teacher writes the note, the skill and the minutes. The pupil administration system returns recent marks. If there is no mark, the note stands and the pass does not invent a gap.
Use the pupil administration system's own plan screen before a new store. A blank activity stays blank.
The stored program is about the pupil's skill, not a score of the teacher. A later edit voids the acceptance.
Upkeep is the two hours allowed below to keep the skill codes and the activity fields current.
unknowns: Whether this school's extra help is recorded as a formal development plan.
The minutes cap, and who besides the teacher and the assistant may open the program.
A Dutch research project plans to draft justifications for formal plans and has published no results.
research_questions: How many extra-help pupils already have a goal code on the pupil record?
How often the parent talk changes the drafted activities?

already_counted.description: Read each drafted activity and reject a diagnosis the note does not state.
Accept the program after the parent talk, before it is stored.

incremental.description: Keep the skill codes and the activity fields the draft may fill.

approvals.approved_version: Remedial program for this pupil and skill, with activity titles and minutes, as the elementary teacher accepted after the parent talk.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most extra help is a one-off chat and the draft is often rejected. High: several pupils share a skill code and the activities are reused after one acceptance. The taught session does not shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assign class work and homework, then grade both.

steps.what: Assign the class work and the homework for tomorrow.
Collect the finished class work and homework.
Mark closed items on the class work by the key.
Suggest a rubric score for each open homework answer.

loop.input: The open homework answer, the item id and the rubric levels the teacher wrote.
loop.output: One rubric level for that answer, or blank.
loop.check: The teacher reads the answer and rejects a level the answer does not show.
loop.stop: One pass. If a sample of five double-marked answers disagrees, the remaining answers stay blank. No second call.
loop.why_not_simpler: The homework answer is free text, so the closed-item key cannot score it.

steps.what: Grade the open homework answers the suggestion missed.
Store the accepted homework grade on the pupil record.

tasks.design: Closed items on class work and homework are marked from the teacher's key in the {OTHER}, the pupil administration system. One pass suggests a rubric score for each open answer; the teacher reads the answer and rejects a score it does not support, and a disagreed sample leaves the rest blank. Only the accepted grade is stored, and it is not released as a mark until then.
tasks.previous_blocker: Open answers were read one by one, and closed items were ticked by hand onto a mark sheet.
tasks.enabler_now: A key marks closed items, and a bounded pass can suggest a rubric level the teacher checks against the answer.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding the grade that counts, and spotting an answer that is right for the wrong reason, stays with the teacher.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher can tell a lucky guess from a pupil who understands.

ambition.what: Return the homework grade on the next school day.

tasks.altitude: Assigning and collecting stay. Closed items and retyping the grade shrink. The teacher still decides every mark that counts.

reach.task: Hand back the accepted class work.
reach.learn: Give back only the grade the teacher stored, and do not change a level.

evidence.claim: CheckMate suggests scores for open questions. Seven teachers tested it. One said 1.5 hours of marking took under 15 minutes; that is his account, not this school's result.
Teacher Tapp in October 2026 reported that 7 percent of secondary teachers use AI for marking.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes is high-risk. A homework grade that counts is that kind of outcome, so the suggestion is not stored as the mark.
That high-risk date is 2 December 2027.
Inferring pupils' emotions is banned. This marking reads the written answer, not a face or a mood.
A school that adapts an AI tool can become its provider.
Texas machine-scored state tests, and rescoring requests rose from 2,758 in 2024 to 64,489 in 2026. Computers had first-scored 58 percent of more than 13,300 raised reading scores.
Closed items with a fixed key can be marked by code. The teacher still writes the key. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The focal boundary is the elementary teacher assigning the work, collecting it, marking it and storing the grade. Pupils' writing time is not this task.

Fields are pupil id, work type class or homework, item id, item kind closed or open, pupil answer, key, rubric level, suggested score and accepted score. The teacher writes the key and the rubric. A closed item with no key stays unmarked. An open answer with no fitting level stays blank.
The teacher sees every open answer that receives a suggestion. Below the sample agreement, the rest are marked by hand in the grade step, which does not shrink.
Use the pupil administration system's mark screen before a new mark book. The stored grade is the pupil's work, not a score of the teacher.
A later change to the score voids the acceptance. Upkeep is the three hours allowed to keep the key and the rubric levels current.
unknowns: Whether homework arrives on paper or in a learning system.
The agreement level the school will set before the rest returns to hand marking.
Whether this homework grade counts on a report.
research_questions: What share of the items are closed and already have a key?
How often the teacher rejects the suggested rubric level?

already_counted.description: Read each open answer against the suggested rubric level.
Mark by hand the open answers the sample sent back, and accept the grade.

incremental.description: Keep the answer key and the rubric levels current for this class.

approvals.approved_version: Homework grade for this pupil and this assignment, with closed-item tally and accepted rubric levels, as the elementary teacher graded.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most items are open and the sample often disagrees, so hand grading stays. High: a large closed-item set marks from the key and most open suggestions survive the reading. Assigning and collecting do not shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare, give and grade tests, then judge progress.

steps.what: Prepare tests and assignments from this week's goals.

loop.input: The teacher's seed item, the goal code and the reading level for this class.
loop.output: A rewritten stem that keeps the same goal code, or the seed unchanged if the rewrite is rejected.
loop.check: The teacher reads the stem and rejects it when it asks a different goal or a harder level than named.
loop.stop: One pass. A rejected stem stays as the teacher's seed. No second call.
loop.why_not_simpler: The seed is a sentence, so a blank template cannot tell which words are too hard for the class.

steps.what: Accept the test paper before the students sit it.
Administer the test while the students write.
Grade closed test items from the answer key.
Draft a mark for each open assignment answer.

loop.input: The open assignment answer, the item id and the rubric levels.
loop.check: The teacher reads the answer and rejects a level the writing does not show.
loop.stop: One pass. Blank if no level fits. If a sample of five disagrees, the other answers stay blank. No second call.
loop.why_not_simpler: The assignment answer is free text, so the answer key cannot mark it.

steps.what: Evaluate students' progress from the marked test.
File the accepted test grade on the pupil record.

tasks.design: The teacher writes a seed item per goal; one pass rewrites the wording, and the teacher rejects a stem that asks a different goal before the pupils sit the test. Closed items are marked from the key, and a second pass suggests a score for each open answer that the teacher checks against the writing. The teacher judges progress, and only that accepted grade is filed on the {OTHER}, the pupil administration system.
tasks.previous_blocker: The paper was retyped from last year, and open answers were scored without the pupil's last marks beside them.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded pass can reword a seed item, and a key can mark the closed items, while the teacher still accepts the paper and the grade.
tasks.still_hard: Judging what the test says about this pupil's progress, and keeping the room fair while they write, stays with the teacher.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher knows which missed item is a bad day and which is a gap to teach next.

ambition.what: Tell a pupil what to practise the day the test is graded.

tasks.altitude: Sitting the test and judging progress stay. Rewording items and filing the grade take less time. The teacher still accepts the paper and the grade.

reach.task: Check that the test still matches the year plan.
reach.learn: Read the goal code on each accepted item, and do not treat a rewritten stem as a new goal.

evidence.claim: LessonUp's lesson editor rewrites text at another level, summarises it and translates it. That supports rewording a seed item, not awarding a grade.
CheckMate suggests scores for open questions. The teacher still sees the answer. One teacher's timing claim is his account.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes or watches tests is high-risk. Administering the test stays with the teacher, and the suggested mark is not the stored grade.
The high-risk obligations apply from 2 December 2027.
Texas machine-scored state reading items, and rescoring requests rose from 2,758 in 2024 to 64,489 in 2026.
Parents and pupils consent to pupil-data rules under the school participation act. A test grade is pupil data.

assumptions: The focal boundary is the elementary teacher preparing the paper, sitting it with the class, grading it and filing the grade. The pupils' writing time is not counted.

Fields are goal code, seed stem, reading level, rewritten stem, answer key, pupil id, item kind, rubric level, score and a progress sentence. The teacher writes the seed, the level, the key and the progress sentence. The pass may only reword a seed or suggest a level. A rejected stem stays the seed. A blank score stays blank.
The progress sentence is the teacher's. It is not drafted. No tool watches the room or infers effort while the test is sat.
Use the pupil administration system's existing grade screen. Native configuration before a new test store. A later change to the score voids the acceptance.
Upkeep is the 2.5 hours allowed to keep goal codes, reading levels and rubric levels current.
unknowns: Whether tests are sat on paper or on a screen.
Which scores count for the report.
The reading-level labels this school already uses.
research_questions: What share of tests are rebuilt from last year's paper rather than a new seed?
How often a rewritten stem changes the goal the teacher checks?

already_counted.description: Read each rewritten stem against the goal and the reading level.
Accept the paper before the class sits it.
Read each open answer against the suggested level.
Judge progress and accept the grade before it is filed.

incremental.description: Keep goal codes, reading levels and rubric levels current.

approvals.approved_version: Test grade and progress note for this pupil and this paper, with the closed-item tally and accepted open levels, as the elementary teacher evaluated.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the paper is mostly reused by hand and most answers are open, so the sample returns them to the teacher. High: seeds are reworded once and many items are closed. Sitting the test and judging progress do not shrink.

tasks.short: Encourage pupils to try harder tasks for later grades.

steps.what: Prepare learning opportunities aimed at the later grades.
Encourage students to explore challenging tasks and persevere.

tasks.design: A fixed catalogue filtered by year group lists learning opportunities for the later grades in the {DOCS}. The teacher may use one item when encouraging a pupil, and may ignore the list. Nothing scores perseverance or reads a face.
tasks.previous_blocker: The next-grade idea lived in the teacher's memory and was easy to skip on a busy day.
tasks.enabler_now: A year-group list can be filtered with ordinary configuration, with no model and no pupil score.
tasks.still_hard: Knowing whether this child should be pushed today stays in the room.
tasks.human_edge: Only the teacher can tell if the child is ready, not merely behind.

ambition.what: Offer one named next-grade task the week a pupil is stuck.

tasks.altitude: The week is still the conversation. The list only makes a next-grade offer easier to remember.

reach.task: See which opportunities the next grade already lists.
reach.learn: Read the year-group list, and do not treat it as a judgement of a child.

evidence.claim: A year-group catalogue of clubs, books and next-grade skills is a filter on titles the school already wrote. It does not judge a child. Model knowledge.
Inferring pupils' emotions is banned. The design does not watch faces or score perseverance.
If the school later stores which child was offered a task, parents and pupils consent to that pupil-data rule under the school participation act. The catalogue itself names no child.

assumptions: The focal boundary is the elementary teacher preparing a short list and encouraging pupils during the lesson. The encouragement does not shrink.

Fields on the catalogue are year group, opportunity id, title and next-grade skill. No pupil id. The school writes the titles. The filter returns titles for that year. An empty year returns an empty list, and the teacher encourages without it.
No perseverance score is stored. If a later change records a named pupil, the consent assumption above applies and this design stops short of that record.
Upkeep is the one hour allowed to refresh titles when the year plan changes. Native document configuration before any new app.
unknowns: Whether the school already keeps a year-group list of clubs and next-grade skills.
Whether any opportunity names a fee or a place outside school.
research_questions: How often a teacher already offers a next-grade task without a list?
Which year groups have titles the school is willing to show a class?

already_counted.description: Glance at the opportunity list while encouraging the pupil.

incremental.description: Refresh catalogue titles when the year plan changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the teacher rarely looks at the list. High: the short prep of remembering opportunities moves to the filter. The conversation in the room does not shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
